title: Short Stuff: The Call is Coming... FROM INSIDE THE HOUSE
summary: Short Stuff episode on the urban legend "The Call is Coming from Inside the House," also known as "The Babysitter and the Man Upstairs." The hosts describe the legend's plot (a babysitter receives escalating prank-like calls from a stranger asking if she checked on the sleeping kids, then learns the call came from inside the house), discuss why it works as a scare given older phone technology, and compare it with other scary legends such as the Hook, The Vanishing Hitchhiker, and "Drip Drop Maniac." The hosts trade personal scare stories. They then recount the 1950 murder of 13-year-old babysitter Janet Chrisman in Columbia, Missouri, which is said to have inspired the legend; suspect Robert Mueller was never charged and the case remains unsolved. The episode closes with films that used the trope, including When a Stranger Calls, Black Christmas, Halloween, Scream, and The Severed Arm (1973).
topics: The Call is Coming from Inside the House

segments.title: The babysitter legend explained
segments.summary: The hosts outline the urban legend, also called 'the babysitter and the man upstairs': a teen babysitter receives escalating calls from a stranger asking if she has checked on the sleeping kids, until the caller reveals the call came from inside the house. They note why it was scarier when phones were limited.

segments.summary: The hosts discuss related legends, including The Vanishing Hitchhiker, The Hook, and Drip Drop Maniac, and the stories they were told as kids.

segments.summary: The hosts swap personal anecdotes about being scared in the dark, sleeping with sheets, and being frightened by family members and roommates during college.

segments.title: Transition to the 1950 murder
segments.summary: The hosts say they will cover the story that may have inspired the legend, a real murder.

segments.title: Janet Chrisman murder in Columbia, Missouri (1950)
segments.summary: In March 1950, 13-year-old Janet Chrisman babysat for Gregory Romack and his wife in Columbia, Missouri. Mister Romack left a loaded shotgun and told her to turn on the porch light before opening the door. Around 10:30 p.m. police got a call from a girl shouting 'come quick' before the line went dead. The Romacks called about thirty minutes later with no answer and found Janet dead when they returned around 1:30 a.m. She had been sexually assaulted and strangled, and the phone had been ripped from the wall.

segments.title: Suspect Robert Mueller and the unsolved case
segments.summary: The Romacks and Janet's family suspected Robert Mueller, a friend of Gregory Romack who had hired Janet before and asked her to babysit that night. He had reportedly groped Mrs. Romack days earlier and made odd remarks after the murder. He was never charged, died in 2006, and the case remains unsolved.

segments.title: Films that used the trope
segments.summary: The hosts say the Janet Chrisman case may have inspired the trope, which appears in films including When a Stranger Calls (1979), Black Christmas, Halloween (1978), and Scream. They say the earliest film use they know of is The Severed Arm (1973), where the call is a murder method rather than a plot device. They also mention the sequel to When a Stranger Calls as a riffable movie.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts wrap up the Short Stuff episode and the show's iHeartRadio production credit plays.
